findings.title: New non-default order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public interface. Adding int order() as an abstract method breaks source and binary compatibility for existing implementations. A pre-compiled third-party CryptoProvider will fail with AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration.detectProvider calls order(). This should be a default method, for example returning a neutral order value, unless an intentional breaking change is accepted.

findings.title: Multiple crypto providers are now selected silently with no deterministic tie-break
findings.body: detectProvider now sorts all discovered CryptoProvider instances by order and returns the first one. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so if more than one is present accidentally, the winner depends on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering. The previous fail-fast behavior was replaced by debug-level logging only, which can silently select the wrong security provider in security-sensitive deployments.

findings.title: Ignored crypto providers are still instantiated and may mutate global security state
findings.body: Provider discovery collects all ServiceLoader providers before choosing one, which instantiates every discovered provider. Some constructors, notably FIPS1402Provider and DefaultCryptoProvider, register JCA security providers and modify global Security properties. If such a provider is discovered but ignored because another provider has equal or higher order, those global side effects remain even though the provider is not the selected CryptoProvider.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an arbitrary keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle
findings.body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of the default KeyStore type. That provider may be SUN or another JCA provider and is not necessarily BouncyCastle. Callers expecting the BouncyCastle provider may use the wrong security provider or get confusing failures. If BouncyCastle is not supported by this provider, the method should fail explicitly or return a documented unsupported value rather than masquerading as a BouncyCastle provider.

findings.title: DER-to-raw ECDSA conversion silently truncates oversized integers
findings.body: integerToBytes copies the last qLength bytes when the encoded integer is longer than qLength. This silently truncates oversized R/S values instead of rejecting them. DER-to-raw ECDSA signature conversion should only strip a single leading zero byte and should reject values that do not fit in the expected fixed length; otherwise malformed signatures are transformed into incorrect raw values instead of causing a validation error.

findings.title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate signature length
findings.body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the provided signature array has at least signLength bytes and that signLength is even. A short or malformed signature causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from System.arraycopy instead of a descriptive IOException. Cryptographic parsing code should validate input lengths and throw an appropriate exception.

findings.title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding is not handled safely
findings.body: readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length BER encoding, but callers are not prepared for that value. readSequence treats -1 as an empty sequence, and readInteger passes -1 to read(), resulting in NegativeArraySizeException. Since DER signatures must not use indefinite length, the decoder should throw IOException when 0x80 is encountered.

findings.title: ECDSA conversion test does not use algorithm-specific curves or verify signatures
findings.body: The test generates one default EC key pair and uses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. JOSE ES256/ES384/ES512 require P-256, P-384 and P-521 respectively, with different signature lengths. Using a default key, likely P-256, for ES512 only exercises padding/round-trip and does not test real P-521 signature sizes. The test also does not verify the converted DER signature with Signature.verify, so it cannot detect semantically invalid conversions.
